Marissa / Kim,

Quick read of their redlines. High-level positions I recommend:

1) Governing law vs. seat: We can accept California substantive law (to keep our risk profile predictable) but insist on an arbitration seat in San Francisco (or New York if they persist) — recommending San Francisco as it aligns with our counsel and is neutral for enforcement under the New York Convention. Suggested wording: "This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of California. The seat of any arbitration shall be San Francisco, California; the arbitration shall be administered under the rules of the AAA (or ICC if they prefer)."

2) Injunctive relief carveout: Agree to a narrow carveout that preserves the right to seek provisional relief in court only for (a) actual or threatened misappropriation of Redwood's intellectual property, and (b) confirmed data-exfiltration that presents imminent risk to HarvestPay's customers; otherwise disputes go to arbitration. Proposed clause: short paragraph preserving emergency equitable relief in courts of competent jurisdiction (with notice to Redwood counsel where practicable).

3) Notice & cure: push back on 7-day blanket cure windows. For non-payment: 14 days. For data/security incidents: immediate notice + 48 hours to confirm, with remedial plan and emergency remedies preserved. For operational/perf defaults: 30 days cure. This stratification is defensible and matches our SLOs.

4) Service/Preservation: Add a short order-form appendix requiring HarvestPay to provide a point of contact and expedited access to audit logs for incidents; limit scope to logs strictly necessary to investigate the incident.

I can draft redline language for each item and produce a consolidated tracked change. Also recommend we avoid naming a specific court for injunctive relief—use "courts of the state where seat is located or federal courts therein".

If Sales wants to concede to NY seat for commercial reasons, note: CA governing law + NY seat is operationally okay but creates some friction with counsel.

I'll do the redline and send a consolidated doc by EOD.

— Karthik
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Karthik — +1 to the stratified cure approach. A couple of practical edits:

- For the injunctive carveout, we should require HarvestPay to certify in writing before seeking emergency judicial relief that they have attempted arbitration emergency mechanisms (e.g., expedited preliminary relief through AAA where available) — this limits forum-shopping.
- Replace "San Francisco" seat language with "Seat: United States (San Francisco, CA)" to avoid unnecessary specificity in the body; keep the detailed venue in the execution block or SOW.
- Preserve our standard limitation on discovery in arbitration for routine disputes; allow broader preservation/discovery only where a court grants injunctive relief or under express written agreement.

I'll review Karthik's redline when it's ready. Also note: procurement may accept NY seat if Sales offers concession on termination rights — flagging that as a negotiation lever.

Kimberly Park
